hints: A particle is not fundamental if it has an internal structure made from smaller particles.
Classify the alpha particle, neutron and proton as composite; compare them with the beta-plus particle, which is a positron.
walkthrough: A proton and a neutron are composite hadrons made from quarks, so neither is fundamental.
An alpha particle is a helium nucleus containing two protons and two neutrons, so it is also composite.
A beta-plus particle is a positron, which is a fundamental lepton.
Therefore the particles in the list that are not fundamental are alpha, neutron and proton.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies all three non-fundamental particles as alpha, neutron and proton, with no beta-plus included.

hints: An electric field exerts force only on a particle with non-zero electric charge.
From the list, identify the particle whose net charge is zero.
walkthrough: The electric force magnitude is F = |q|E, so a particle with zero net charge has no electric force in an electric field.
Alpha particles, beta-plus particles and protons are positively charged.
A neutron has zero net charge, so the neutron is the only listed particle that experiences no electric force.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the neutron as the particle that experiences no electric force in an electric field.

hints: The neutron has zero charge; compare the charged particles using both charge magnitude and mass.
A beta-plus particle is a positron with charge +e and a mass far smaller than a proton or alpha particle.
walkthrough: The neutron has zero charge, so its charge-to-mass ratio is zero.
A proton has charge +e and the alpha particle has charge +2e but about four times the proton mass, so neither has an exceptionally large ratio.
A beta-plus particle has charge +e but the very small electron mass.
Therefore beta-plus has the largest charge-to-mass ratio.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies beta-plus or β⁺ as the particle with the largest charge-to-mass ratio.

hints: An antidown quark has the opposite charge to a down quark, so its charge is +⅓e.
Subtract this from the hadron's total charge +e, then identify the quark flavour with the remaining charge.
walkthrough: A down quark has charge −⅓e, so an antidown quark has charge +⅓e.
The two-quark hadron has total charge +e, so the other quark must have charge +e − ⅓e = +⅔e.
The quark flavour with charge +⅔e is the up quark.
Therefore the other quark is an up quark, u.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the antidown quark has charge +⅓e.
Determines that the other quark must have charge +e − ⅓e = +⅔e.
Identifies the other quark as an up quark or u.
